source_name: ECB – List of Monetary Financial Institutions (MFI list), Slovakia subset
why_relevant: Daily-updated, machine-readable list of MFIs including SK credit institutions and money market funds, with stable identifiers. Ideal reference spine for joining SK entity data across sources.

source_name: Obchodný register SR (Slovak Commercial Register, Ministry of Justice)
why_relevant: Legal-entity backbone: IČO, legal form, statutory bodies, shareholders, deposited documents for every SK company including banks, PIs, fintechs and their local subsidiaries. Since 2021 it also records beneficial owners (non-public part). Essential for resolving register names to legal entities.

source_name: Register právnických osôb (RPO) – Statistical Office REST API
why_relevant: Reference register consolidating ORSR, trade register and other source registers since Nov 2017, with a public JSON REST API under CC BY 4.0. The cleanest legal route to bulk entity resolution for every SK actor discovered elsewhere.

source_name: Register účtovných závierok (RÚZ) – Open API
why_relevant: Mandatory filing register of financial statements and annual reports for all SK accounting units, with a documented bulk Open API. Turns the register list of supervised actors into a financially quantified actor map (size, growth, exits).

source_name: NBS – Zoznam účastníkov platobného systému SIPS / TARGET-SK
why_relevant: Participant lists for the domestic retail payment system SIPS and for TARGET-SK. Identifies which institutions actually clear and settle in SK — a sharper commercial map than licence lists alone.

source_name: NBS – Štatistika: Banky (banking statistics landing)
why_relevant: Statistical reporting population of SK banks; the reporting-agent lists and aggregates implicitly enumerate the active credit-institution universe and give the supervisory reporting calendar.

source_name: NBS – Register správcov alternatívnych investičných fondov (AIFM register)
why_relevant: Register of registered/authorised AIF managers in SK — completes the supervised-entity perimeter beyond banking and payments for a sector=both scope.

source_name: ÚVO – Register konečného užívateľa výhod / registers of economic operators
why_relevant: Public Procurement Office registers of economic operators and their beneficial owners — an alternative ownership-transparency pointer and the bridge between register data and public-sector contracting by banks/payment vendors.

source_name: data.gov.sk / data.slovensko.sk – Slovak open data catalogue (register datasets)
why_relevant: National open-data catalogue that indexes register datasets (RPO, ORSR extracts, procurement, statistics) with explicit licences — the discovery layer for legally reusable bulk register data.

source_name: micascan.eu – pan-European MiCA CASP lookup (referenced by NBS)
why_relevant: Aggregator of national MiCA authorisations that NBS itself points investors to for verifying platform legitimacy; useful as a cross-check and for spotting SK-passported CASPs. Aggregator, so treat as secondary to NBS/ESMA registers.

source_name: SBA — Členovia / Members list
why_relevant: Authoritative roster of banks and branches of foreign banks operating in SK plus associate members. POINTER data: seeds the whole private-bank actor map for other workstreams (vendor wins, tenders, PSD2/instant-payments rollouts) and lets you attribute positions to specific institutions.

source_name: SBA — Projekty a štandardy (self-regulatory projects & standards)
why_relevant: Where SBA documents sector-level self-regulation and shared infrastructure/standards (e.g. the SBA Institute of Alternative Dispute Resolution, codes, common standards). Self-regulatory standards often pre-empt or implement EU payments rules and are a leading indicator of what banks will require from vendors.

source_name: EBF — Slovakia country page (SBA in the European federation)
why_relevant: SBA has been an EBF and European Payment Council member since 1996. The EBF country page and EBF position papers carry the English-language framing of Slovak bank positions on EU files (PSD3/PSR, instant payments, digital euro, AMLR) and give comparable cross-country context.

source_name: EU Transparency Register / LobbyFacts datacard — Slovenská banková asociácia
why_relevant: Reveals-indirectly source: registered lobbying declarations expose which EU legislative files SBA declares an interest in, budget, staff and meetings — an early signal of which regulatory dossiers the Slovak banking sector is actively working, independent of what SBA chooses to publish.

source_name: Slovenská FinTech asociácia (Slovak FinTech Association)
why_relevant: Founded Aug 2018; explicitly a platform for communication between fintech entities and regulators, forming working groups and holding open discussions with government. Founding member of EDFA. Publishes blog/news and thematic sections (crypto & blockchain) that track MiCA, sandbox and payments regulation debate earlier and more candidly than banks.

source_name: Slovenská FinTech asociácia — Členovia / Členstvo
why_relevant: Member roster of the Slovak fintech/payments ecosystem — the pointer that maps non-bank PSPs, e-money firms, crypto and infrastructure vendors active in SK. Membership page plus the separate 'Členstvo' page for joining criteria.

source_name: Slov-Lex — legislatívne procesy / hromadné pripomienky (association comments on drafts)
why_relevant: Since April 2016 all inter-ministerial comment procedures (MPK) are run here. Association comments — including bulk/collective comments (hromadné pripomienky) — are filed and published per LP/YYYY/NNN case with their disposition. This is the authoritative, timestamped record of what each association actually asked for and what the ministry accepted, plus the statutory comment deadlines.

source_name: LRV — Legislatívna rada vlády SR: vyhodnotenie MPK documents
why_relevant: Publishes the 'Vyhodnotenie medzirezortného pripomienkového konania' documents that list every commenting body (SLASPO, SBA, employer unions, etc.), their exact comment text, and whether it was accepted — a compact, machine-parseable record of association influence on financial-sector drafts.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia poisťovní (SLASPO)
why_relevant: Interest association of commercial insurers; activities explicitly focused on legislation, insurance economics, education. Relevant to sector=both because insurers are co-affected by IRRD, DORA, AML and distribution rules, and SLASPO appears as a named commenter in MPK evaluation documents.

source_name: Slovenská asociácia správcovských spoločností (SASS)
why_relevant: Association of SK asset-management companies (est. 1998) whose stated priority is cooperation with state legislative bodies in drafting financial-market legal norms. Explicitly names SBA and AOCP as partner associations — useful cross-link for the actor map.

source_name: AFISP — Asociácia finančných sprostredkovateľov a finančných poradcov
why_relevant: Est. 2007, unites ~17 members representing ~62% of financial agents in SK. Central voice on distribution/commission regulation (e.g. the commission-cap debate), consumer-protection rules and the Retail Investment Strategy — directly a regulation/consultation source and a pointer to the intermediary ecosystem.

source_name: Asociácia leasingových spoločností SR (ALS SR)
why_relevant: Est. 1992; analyses legal norms governing leasing, reacts to practice and proposes solutions; publishes a Code of Ethics (self-regulation) and a full member directory. Leasing/consumer-credit regulation and CCD2 implementation touch the same bank-owned finance houses.

source_name: ASINS — Asociácia slovenských inkasných spoločností
why_relevant: Est. 2010; unites major creditors, debt-collection and auction firms; explicitly advocates ethical collection at national and European level and 'fair legislation in debt management'. Relevant to NPL, consumer-credit and debt-collection regulation affecting banks.

source_name: Republiková únia zamestnávateľov (RÚZ)
why_relevant: Most representative SK employer organisation (1,300+ members). Files formal positions in MPK and tripartite on financial-sector and AML drafts; banks and financial firms route positions through it. URL inferred from the organisation's common domain — treat as unverified until liveness pass.

source_name: FinStat — association legal-entity and financial records (SBA, SFA, SLASPO, ALS, ASINS)
why_relevant: Aggregator of SK register data: gives each association's IČO, statutory bodies, founding date, financial statements and an 'Udalosti' change feed. Useful to validate that an association is live and active, and to detect governance changes (new president = new lobbying posture).

source_name: Slovenská banková asociácia — LinkedIn page
why_relevant: Associations frequently post position summaries, event announcements and staff/expert commentary on LinkedIn before or instead of the website; also identifies named policy staff (useful for attribution and for tracking who speaks on payments files).

source_name: Slovenská FinTech asociácia — Facebook channel
why_relevant: Primary announcement channel for the fintech association's events, working-group calls and consultation activity; often more current than the website.

source_name: Blockchain Slovakia / Slovenská kryptomenová asociácia (SKMA)
why_relevant: Crypto/blockchain self-organising bodies. SKMA is described as a non-profit focused on education, regulation and legislative support, and consumer protection — a natural commenter on MiCA/DAC8/stablecoin (EMT) implementation in SK payments. Blockchain Slovakia's canonical domain is inferred from its brand; only its Facebook page was directly observed, so treat the URL as unverified.

source_name: EDFA — European Digital Finance Association (SFA is a founding member)
why_relevant: The Slovak FinTech Association is a founding member of EDFA; EDFA publishes European-level fintech/payments position papers and cooperation agreements (e.g. with Finnovating) that carry SK fintech positions into EU consultations. English-language framing of SK fintech asks. Domain inferred from the acronym — unverified.
